title: Knowledge-aware supply: push what memory lacks, leave the rest one read away, let memory speak marked, and check it by script against the early entries and the construction guard
summary: Phase 1's dilution lesson splits into four separate effects, and each one needs a different fix. (1) An instruction confound. Dictionary-fed arms that were allowed Quran memory (the v11 brief) cite a median of 30 outside-surah passages (range 12–47, n=16). The same inputs without that permission give 1.5 (10 of 24 runs cite none). The cold arm gives 10.5. Once permission is fixed, input size no longer predicts outside reach (Spearman −0.03). (2) Real bulk dilution, but only above about 140k billed tokens: thinking collapses only in the package arms. (3) A contaminated test. The shared brief's example citation "(15:26, 15:28, 15:33)" in write_v10.md line 59 and write_v11.md line 112 is exactly the ḥamaʾ partner set for 18:86. So "every run, cold included, recalls the ḥamaʾ passages" is not evidence of memory. (4) Real memory gaps with a clear, scriptable shape. I labelled by hand every lexical claim in the 13 fully annotatable cold readings (344 non-plain branches). Memory reaches 35% of branches in positions B001–B003 but only 3% of B004+. It reaches 21% of branches with 4–6 early sources but 4–5% of those with 1–3. It reaches 0 of the 60 branches that no HFT or v12 reader ever activated, and 1 of 56 collocation branches. Its Quran parallels are thematic: only 1.24% of 299,657 memory suggestions share a root of ≤30 uses with the focus ayah, against 7.8% of retrieved pairs. Nearly all the phrases it quotes are real: 12 of 14 non-Quran Arabic tags in the cold readings are in the six early entries. Phase 1's "7 phrases found nowhere" came from checking against truncated packet text. My design has four parts. A free three-feature score per branch (position, early-source count, activation history; AUC 0.88 on those labels, in-sample) decides which branches get their early phrases pushed. Every branch still keeps an index line, so nothing is dropped. Collocation-bound branches always carry their construction. Roots with ≤30 uses get every use pushed at root level; this reaches 15:26/28/33 for 18:86, which v15's per-lemma concordance misses. Partner-by-form profiles show dominant roles (nafakha: active verb with rūḥ in 5 of 9 attachments; passive with ṣūr). The whole surah is pushed as a cached prefix for 113 of the 114 surahs. The synthesis call is allowed memory and asked to mark it, and gets no audit instructions. A script verifier runs afterwards. It found memory to be no worse than the dictionary-fed arm on the construction guard: 1 unscoped use (arḍ kanūd applied to insān) against 4 for the dictionary arm, which never saw branch_kind. The resulting packets are 16–93k tokens, under the collapse zone, and hold every watch-case ingredient tested. An optional one-time knowledge-gap probe would replace the static score with measured Opus recall for about $26–51 through the Batch API.
answers:
Q2a (main). Model memory is enough for the following, so push nothing and verify afterwards:
- Quran references and thematic cross-surah parallels. Memory Quran suggestions are 92.5% cross-surah, 52% share only frequent roots, and 1.24% share a ≤30-use root. Permitted fed arms cite 12–47 outside passages.
- Primary senses, and secondary senses in the early branch positions of well-known words. Memory's latent recall is 35% for B001–B003 and 46% for branches with score 3. Examples: ṣirāṭ/saraṭa, ḍālla, ṭarīq muʿabbad, ḍabḥ B003 (fire), kanūd, ʿaṣr B002/B003, mirfaq/irtifāq, dayn, hādī/hadiyya.
- Classical phrases for those senses: 12 of 14 cold non-Quran tags are attested in the six early entries, for example kamā tadīnu tudān and ḍalla l-māʾu fī l-laban (Tahdhīb).
- The construction scope of famous cases. Both 4:34 cold arms rule out ḍaraba = travel because it needs fī.
- Grammar and Turkish drift.

Data must supply the rest:
- Minor and rare branches, with their early phrases: B004+ at 3%, 1–3 sources at 4–5%, never-activated at 0%. The watch-case examples are sabal B010, ʿayn B008 (the sun disk), qawm B012, mālik B006/B008 and ṣudūd B013 (kohl).
- Construction tags. Memory, like the dictionary arm that lacked branch_kind, applied arḍ kanūd to insān at 100:6.
- Root-level concordance for low-frequency roots, and partner profiles for mid-frequency ones. The cold arm missed 15:29, 38:72 and 32:9 for nafakha; memory suggestions never contain the loaded-word partners; the inter-ayah labels grade them "no value" or "medium".
- The surah text, which is where the cold arm's same-surah reach came from.
- The project's own chains, which memory cannot hold.

Dilution. It is real only for bulk packages of ≥140k billed tokens: thinking fell 45k→9k, 42k→8k and 29k→11k. Below that, the drop in outside reach was the "work only from the supplied evidence" clause, and the "cold beats dict" gap (8 against 5 anchors) is inside replicate noise (Jaccard 0.60). The knowledge-aware packet stays at 16–93k tokens.

Q2b, from this angle. The existing labels are enough to set a rule but not to train one:
- 344 hand-labelled branch cases with 41 positives in 13 ayat (recall_manual.tsv);
- about 100 [recall] marks in v11/v12, mostly Quran references;
- 299,657 memory rows from the GPT inter-ayah runs, which measure GPT, not Opus.

The proposed probe would give about 11.4k branch labels, 1,633 root count and dominant-role labels, and construction-drift labels for Opus directly. Any learned policy only decides what gets pushed; the index line guarantees nothing is dropped.

Also bears on:
- Q1: the brief contamination and the three Phase 1 detector artefacts are corrections to what we thought we knew.
- Q4: this is the supply layer that "synthesize free, anchor afterward" needs.

stages.name: 0a. Branch supply table
stages.input: quran-data/data/dictionary/tr/*_entry.json (branch position, sources, branch_kind + scope note, early phrases); HFT and v12 activation counts (../branch_table.py)
stages.output: Per branch: memory_score 0–3 = [B001–B003] + [≥4 of 6 early sources] + [HFT+v12 ≥10]; a construction tag for collocation/non_bare branches (C[first early phrase]); the phrase to push when score ≤1
stages.size_or_tokens: 11,392 Quranic branches: 61% get phrases pushed, 22% get a construction tag

stages.name: 0b. Uses and partner index
stages.output: For roots ≤30 uses: every use as keyword-in-context. For roots with ≥3 uses: partners by form with counts (e.g. ن ف خ PV:I with ر و ح 5/9; PV_PASS with ص و ر 6/8; ح م أ with ص ل ص ل 3/3)

stages.name: 0c. Optional knowledge-gap probe (needs approval)
stages.who: Opus 5.5 at effort low through the Batch API (pilot: 30 roots × effort low/high via claude -p); scored by script (character n-grams, with local E5 models from quran-slm later) plus an optional Luna mapping pass
stages.input: Per root: the root letters and its Quranic surface forms only (no dictionary). Ask for every sense known from the early lexicons, with a classical phrase, any construction it needs, the Quran use count, the dominant use and 2–3 references
stages.output: Per branch: recalled y/n; phrase attested y/n; construction drift (a collocation sense claimed as bare). Per root: count error; dominant role hit. This replaces memory_score (not recalled → push; recalled → index line only)
stages.size_or_tokens: ~350 input and ~1.5–3k output tokens per root
stages.stance: measurement job; its output never enters a synthesis prompt

stages.name: 1. Knowledge-aware packet
stages.input: Stage 0 tables; v15 loaders (text, words, qirāʾāt, channel index)
stages.output: The whole surah (window plus same-surah list for S2); the ayah's words; every branch of its roots as one line (id | image | Turkish gloss), plus early phrases when score ≤1, plus the construction tag; rare branches of neighbour roots within ±3 ayat; root-level uses and partners; same-surah occurrences; chain-map lines anchored at the ayah; variant readings; pull paths. No verdicts, grades or construction-presence status
stages.size_or_tokens: billed tokens: 1:6 15.5k; 29:38 33.7k; 18:86 44.8k; 18:96 48.0k; 4:34 81.1k; 2:282 80.9k; 5:6 92.7k (the surah text is a cached prefix)

stages.name: 2. Synthesis
stages.who: Opus 5.5 at effort high (whichever generative step Phase 2 adopts: A/B)
stages.output: Record and/or reading, with memory-sourced senses, phrases, counts and reports marked [memory]
stages.size_or_tokens: output uncapped (cold arms 15–60k tokens including thinking)
stages.stance: generative. Memory permitted; no audit or checklist instructions; a neutral citation-format example

stages.name: 3. Verification
stages.who: script (verify_memory.py prototype, plus v11 verify_src.py / v15 check.py for Quran quotes)
stages.input: Synthesis output; full early entries (dictionary/data/output/root_packets entry_text_clean); dictionary branch fields; Quran text; C2 construction index
stages.output: V1 each non-Quran Arabic phrase → early:<source> | dictionary-branch | not-found (→ memory mark). V2 each construction-bound sense → construction present at the focus | cited at its own locus | FLAG. V3 each Quran reference and quotation checked. V4 unmarked lexical claims that match no branch → marked. All marks are appended; nothing is deleted

stages.name: 4. Second look at flags only
stages.input: Each V2 flag with its branch, scope note, early phrases and focus ayah
stages.output: Is the construction present at the focus: yes / no / partial, with the words quoted. For example, ḍabḥ B002 (foreleg stride) at 100:1 has horses as subject, so the flag is probably false
stages.once_or_per_ayah: per ayah, only where flags exist (0–4 per reading observed)
stages.size_or_tokens: a few hundred tokens per flag

stages.name: 5. Render and record
stages.who: script plus the writer step of the chosen pipeline
stages.output: Marks shown in the app. Senses whose construction is absent go to the record's set-aside list with the reason (nothing lost silently)

data_processing.method: Top partners per form with attach counts, printed descriptively
Whole surah when ≤40k tokens (every surah except S2 at 61k); same-surah root occurrences for roots ≤400 uses

data_processing.cost: free; a cached prefix in production

north_star_coverage.how: Whole-surah text for 113 of 114 surahs (the cold arm's same-surah reach came from it); same-surah root occurrences; ±3 neighbour rare branches
Chain-map lines anchored at the ayah are pushed as a starting point to ground and extend, never rediscovered; the probe and scripts do not build chains
Root-level uses plus partner-by-form counts make the recurring role visible without an interpretation (nafakha with rūḥ 5/9; ḥamaʾ with ṣalṣāl 3/3)
Memory is permitted, so QeQ reach returns (fed and permitted arms: 12–47 outside refs), and V3 checks every reference afterwards
Every branch of every root stays visible, so a root's branches can be read as one concept; rare branches carry quotable early phrases
No model selects or drops anything; the policy only adds; flags annotate and never delete; failed construction checks go to set-aside with the reason
Each finding stays anchored to a dictionary branch; V1 attests phrases against the six early entries; memory is marked by the model and by script
Nothing is lost silently: full lists stay pullable, and set-asides are recorded
The construction guard keeps collocation senses off the plain reading (ḍaraba at 4:34), which protects the ground
Packets of 16–93k tokens (the surah as a cached prefix) cost about $0.2–0.7 per synthesis call through Batch; verification by script is free
Turkish drift is left to memory: loanword cards stay pullable, not pushed (untested whether pushing helps)

cost.per_ayah_test_cli: One KA synthesis call on the subscription (claude -p bills input as a 1-hour cache write at $8/M and output at $20/M; output assumed 20–45k including thinking): 1:6 ≈ $0.5; 29:38 ≈ $0.9; 18:86 and 18:96 ≈ $1.0–1.3; 4:34 and 5:6 ≈ $1.5–1.7. Verification by script: $0. Luna second look: only where flags exist (0–4 per reading), estimated < $0.05 (Luna runs are unpriced in the ledger).
cost.per_ayah_production_api: Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per MTok, Batch −50% (stacks with caching), cache read $0.20/M, 1-hour cache write 2×. Surah text as a shared cached prefix ≈ $0.004 per ayah read (one write per surah: ≤38k tokens × $8/M × 0.5 ≈ $0.15, amortized). Ayah-specific part 10–55k tokens × $2/M = $0.02–0.11. Output 20–60k × $10/M = $0.20–0.60. That is ≈ $0.2–0.7 per synthesis call, or ≈ $0.5–1.4 per ayah if the pipeline has two Opus calls (discover + write) on the same supply. Verification: $0 plus Luna flags ≈ $0.01–0.05.
cost.one_time: Branch supply table, uses and partner index, KA builder and verifier: scripts only (prototypes exist), about 1–2 days to harden. Optional probe: pilot of 30 roots × effort low/high on the subscription ≈ $3–9 list-equivalent; full probe of 1,633 roots through Batch ≈ $26–51 (≈350 input and 1.5–3k output tokens per root), plus an optional Luna mapping pass ≤ ~$5 (estimate).
cost.assumptions: Token counts come from a calibration fitted to 41 billed single-turn v9 runs (calib.py: tokens ≈ 4,581 + 1.151 × Arabic chars + 0.366 × other chars; median error 0.8%). Output sizes are taken from the v9 cold arms (15–60k). Pricing is from the claude-api skill (Opus 5.5 $4/$20; cache read $0.20; writes 1.25× (5 min) or 2× (1 h); Batch 50% stacking with caching; cache hits inside a concurrent batch are best-effort, so submit each surah's first ayah before the rest). Luna costs are estimates (Luna ≈ 40× cheaper than Opus per the project).

experiments_run.method: Parsed the evidence clauses in v9/lines/synth.py and the evidence sentences of write_v10.md and write_v11.md. Grouped the 58 Phase 1 metrics rows as COLD (18), FED-NOPERM (24) and FED-PERM (16: v11 brief, dictionary-fed, 'The Quran itself, from the files and from your own knowledge of the whole Quran'); compared ayah by ayah; Spearman of input against outside refs within each group
experiments_run.result: Median outside-surah refs: COLD 10.5 (3–28), FED-NOPERM 1.5 (0–38; zero in 10 of 24), FED-PERM 30 (12–47; zero in none), e.g. 1:6 cold 12 / dict 0 / v11 42. Within FED-PERM, input size does not predict outside refs (rho −0.03); within FED-NOPERM it does (rho 0.74, because packages carry related-passage lists). Across all fed runs, rho(permission, outside) = 0.67. Thinking medians by billed input: 14.1k (0–50k), 26.6k (50–150k), 20.3k (>150k). The collapse is specific to the 140–420k package arms. Also found: the example citation '(15:26, 15:28, 15:33)' in write_v10.md:59, write_v11.md:112, v10/prompts/write.md:59 and v11/prompts/write.md:113 is the 18:86 watch set, and every w10/v11 18:86 run cites exactly those three

experiments_run.what: (1) What memory recalls unaided, by branch class
experiments_run.method: Manually annotated every lexical-claim sentence of the cold readings (../r2/lex_claims_w10-opus-cold.txt) against the dictionary branches of each ayah's identity roots, for the 13 fully annotatable ayat (1:1–1:7, 18:86, 100:1, 100:6, 100:10, 103:1, 103:2): 392 branches, 48 plain, 344 latent candidates. Compared with the dictionary-fed arms' Arabic-token hits (Phase 1 q2a_branches.tsv; a lower bound for the fed arms)
experiments_run.result: Cold latent recall 41 of 344 (11.9%); fed ≥66 (19.2%); both 29, cold-only 12, fed-only 37. By position: B001–B003 35%, B004+ 3%. By early sources: 4–6 at 21%, 2–3 at 4%, 1 at 5%. By HFT/v12 activation: ≥10 at 21%, <10 at 2%, never 0 of 60. By kind: mixed 21%, bare 9%, collocation 1 of 56, non_bare 0 of 19. By root frequency: 0–1 words 33% (hapax roots are discussed in tafsir: ḍabḥ B003, kanūd, ḥ-ṣ-l B002). Corrects Phase 1's '105 of 109 branches only when fed' (an Arabic-script detector artefact; e.g. ḍabḥ B003 fire-scorching was recalled in Turkish)

experiments_run.method: memory_score = [B001–B003] + [≥4 sources] + [HFT+v12 ≥10], evaluated on the manual labels, then applied to the whole dictionary
experiments_run.result: Cold recall by score: 0 → 0/96, 1 → 2/112, 2 → 13/80, 3 → 26/56; AUC 0.88 (in-sample, thresholds chosen after seeing the table). Pushing phrases at score ≤1 covers 60% of latent branches with only 2 of 41 memory positives among them (redundant pushes). 17 fed-only branches stay index-only, mostly plain-adjacent senses of frequent roots (e.g. ح س ن B001, ء خ ذ B001). Whole dictionary: 61% of 11,392 Quranic branches pushed, 22% construction-tagged. Watch branches: sabal B010, ʿayn B008, ṣudūd B013, qawm B012, mālik B006/B008 are pushed; ḥamaʾ B001, nafakha B001 and ḍaraba B002 get index lines (their ingredients come from the uses section)

experiments_run.what: (2) Packet sizes and watch ingredients: KA vs cold vs v15 vs full package
experiments_run.method: Built KA packets in four modes (full, phrase, lean, index) for 1:6, 4:34, 5:6, 18:86, 18:96, 29:38 and 2:282. Built v15 ayah packets for ayat v15 never ran with v15 build_ayah redirected to scratch. Token estimates use the calibrated formula. Diacritic-folded ingredient checks

KA-phrase holds every pushed ingredient tested (29:38 6 of 6 including kohl ṣ-d-d B013; 18:86 4 of 4; 18:96 8 of 8; 1:6 6 of 6; 4:34 4 of 4; 5:6 4 of 4). Index mode loses the sabal phrase, ʿayn's gloss and the husband-nushūz phrase; lean loses the sabal phrase

experiments_run.what: Dictionary principle in memory: verification prototype on the existing readings
experiments_run.method: V1: every non-Quran Arabic tag in 18 cold and 12 dict readings matched against the full six early entries (root_packets entry_text_clean) and the dictionary branch fields. V2: every collocation/non_bare branch sense statement checked for its construction at the focus occurrence (partner of the branch's own early phrase within ±3 tokens of the root word) or at a cited locus
experiments_run.result: Cold: 575 tags = 561 Quran + 12 early-attested + 2 unmatched, both constructed grammar examples (نعبدك; a rewritten variant). Phase 1's 'found nowhere' phrases are attested: كما تدين تدان (Tahdhīb), ضل الماء في اللبن (Tahdhīb; not 'reversed': Maqāyīs has the other order), غضبان. Dict: 428 tags, 2 unmatched (root-letter strings). Construction guard: cold 4 statements, 3 scoped at their own locus (ḍaraba travel ×2 via 4:94/4:101; nashaza 58:11) and 1 FLAG (arḍ kanūd at 100:6). Dict 5 statements, 4 FLAGs (ḥamd B005, malaka B005 kneading, ḍabḥ B002, which is probably a false flag, kanūd B003). No memory-specific drift beyond the guard missing from every input

experiments_run.what: Inter-ayah memory suggestions as a free probe of Quran-parallel recall
experiments_run.method: All 6,236 focus files: rows 101+ (memory) against rows 1–100 (retrieval) against random pairs. Share of a content root (excluding roots >1,500 uses) and of low-frequency roots; watch partners
experiments_run.result: Memory rows 299,657: 52.4% share a content root, 4.85% a ≤60-use root, 1.24% a ≤30-use root. Retrieval rows: 72.5%, 16.6%, 7.8%. Random: 18.8%, 0.72%, 0.23%. Memory rows are graded strong/medium in 96%. Watch partners appear only as retrieval rows, with canonical grades: 18:86 → 15:26/28/33 'no value'; 18:96 → 15:29/38:72 'medium'; 5:6 → 5:95/5:97 'no value'; 29:38 → 29:41 'weak'. 32:9, 3:49, 5:110, 21:91 and 66:12 are absent for 18:96

experiments_run.what: Can the probe be scored by script? (mapper feasibility)
experiments_run.method: Character 3-gram cosine: each branch's Arabic definition as a query against image + early phrases of every branch of its root (definition excluded)
experiments_run.result: Top-1 96.1% (chance 13.9%); roots with 10+ branches 94.9% (chance 7.9%). This is an optimistic upper bound, since model paraphrases differ from dictionary wording. The E5 query encoder could not be run (no torch in any available environment; the quran-slm venv interpreter link is broken)

validation_plan.success_criterion: KA packets and a script scorecard frozen for 6 named ayat (1:6, 4:34, 5:6, 18:86, 18:96, 29:38) and 6 blind ayat drawn by script from held-out surahs with channel reviews (never named cases). A brief lint confirms no watch refs or words. One evidence clause shared by every arm: memory permitted, memory marked, a neutral citation example, no audit instructions

validation_plan.step: V1: cold vs KA, same brief, 2 replicates (needs approval)
validation_plan.model_runs: Opus 5.5 at effort high via claude -p: 12 ayat × 2 arms × 2 replicates = 48 calls
validation_plan.success_criterion: Scored blind to arm by script: rare-branch activations (score ≤1 branches anchored and verified by V1/V2), loaded-word partners (predefined, never in prompts), outside and same-surah refs, memory marks, V1/V2 flags, thinking tokens. KA beats cold on rare-branch and loaded-word ingredients by more than the replicate-to-replicate difference (cold-vs-cold ref Jaccard ~0.6 sets the noise band) and is not below cold − noise on same-surah refs. Then the user's own blind pairwise reading of one replicate per arm (compare-myself rule; no comparison agents)
validation_plan.cost: ≈ $3 per ayah list-equivalent (cold ≈ $0.5, KA ≈ $1.0 per call) ≈ $36; every call < $5

validation_plan.step: V2: does bulk dilute? KA vs KA+bulk (needs approval)
validation_plan.model_runs: 4 ayat (4:34, 5:6, 18:96, where thinking collapsed before, plus 1 blind) × 2 replicates of KA+bulk (v9 package appended: 150–400k tokens); reuses V1's KA runs
validation_plan.success_criterion: Dilution is confirmed only if thinking falls by more than 40% and ingredient hits fall beyond the replicate noise, with the evidence clause identical across arms

validation_plan.model_runs: 30 roots stratified by frequency and branch count × effort {low, high} via claude -p = 60 calls
validation_plan.success_criterion: The script mapper reaches ≥ 0.8 precision on my hand check of the 30 roots; low- and high-effort recall sets agree (Jaccard ≥ 0.8) → run the full probe at low effort; the construction-drift rate is measured

validation_plan.step: V4: full probe and policy refit (needs approval)
validation_plan.model_runs: Batch API over 1,633 roots, then a V1-style re-run (KA with the probe-based policy vs KA with the static policy) on 6 new blind ayat × 2 replicates
validation_plan.success_criterion: The probe policy pushes fewer redundant phrases without losing ingredient hits; the static score's AUC against probe labels is reported (an out-of-sample check of the 0.88)

risks.risk: The static score is fitted in-sample on 13 ayat of famous surahs (S1, S100, S103, S18)
risks.mitigation: Every branch keeps an index line (nothing dropped). The probe (V3/V4) gives out-of-sample labels. The push threshold is deliberately generous (61% of branches)

risks.risk: Probe recall in isolation is not activation in context (29:38 needs the neighbours seen together)
risks.mitigation: Use it asymmetrically: not recalled → push; recalled → index line only. Measure in-context activation in V1

risks.risk: The model under-marks memory: v11/v12 used [recall] mostly for Quran refs; cold arms marked nothing
risks.mitigation: V1/V4 mark by script regardless (phrase attestation, sense statements that match no branch); the marking count is a V1 metric

risks.risk: The construction check is weak (C2 index recall 0.21–0.46; my partner-proximity rule misses semantic subjects, e.g. ḍabḥ B002)
risks.mitigation: Kept out of the generative packet (no verdicts); flags get only a Luna second look and are annotated, never deleted; failures go to set-aside with the reason

risks.risk: The user's guard may forbid labelled analogies such as arḍ kanūd for insān, or may allow them
risks.mitigation: Flag them and ask the user; the script keeps both options (FLAG class) without changing the synthesis brief

risks.risk: KA packets for S3–S9 (whole surah up to 38k tokens) reach 81–93k tokens, which is untested with a permission brief
risks.mitigation: Below every observed collapse (≥140k package arms); FED-PERM runs at 90–226k kept 33k median thinking. V1 measures it; fallback to window text plus the same-surah list

risks.risk: Contaminated named cases (S1 answers leaked into earlier prompts; the 18:86 refs in old briefs) inflate the named results
risks.mitigation: Blind ayat in V1, V2 and V4; the brief lint; results reported separately for named and blind ayat

risks.risk: Effect of Turkish-loss supply is unknown (loanword cards left pullable)
risks.mitigation: Score NS2 in V1; add a cards-pushed variant only if KA underperforms v15 on the Turkish layer

extra.brief_contamination: write_v10.md:59, write_v11.md:112, v10/prompts/write.md:59 and v11/prompts/write.md:113 all use the example '(15:26, 15:28, 15:33)', the 18:86 watch partners
wording_principles: Permission: 'Your own knowledge of Arabic and of the whole Quran is open to you beyond what is supplied.' The same clause in every step and every test arm.
Marking as output format: 'Mark a sense, phrase, count or report that you take from memory rather than from the supplied material with [memory].' No request to check, list or account.
Informational only: 'Quotations and references are checked afterwards against the canonical text and the early dictionaries.' No audit, verdict or checklist instructions in the generative call.
A legend, not a rule list: 'C[…] shows the construction a branch belongs to; F[…] a form it belongs to.' Stated once as data semantics, never case-specific.
Supplied data is descriptive only: counts, uses, partners, branch lines. No grades ('no value', 'strong'), no 'never the plain sense' lines, no ranked relevance, no must-land lists, no caps.
No watch-case refs, words or North Star examples anywhere in a brief (a neutral '(S:A, S:A)' citation example), enforced by a lint script.
